managers.message_to_team: The memo says to write a note on cups whenever you can, and it needs to be something personal to that customer—not just a smiley. Please do it on every order today, and keep the window moving; I’ll check in on cups during the shift.
managers.private_thought: With one person out and the timer report watched every morning, this may slow us down, but I’d rather follow the memo as written and manage the pace.

managers.message_to_team: If there’s a natural moment while the line is short, add a quick note that’s actually personal to the customer—not just a smiley. Don’t slow the handoff or leave your station short for it, and skip it when we’re in a rush.
managers.private_thought: Nice if it makes someone’s day, but with one person out I’m not trading throughput for extra steps that aren’t measured.

managers.message_to_team: If you’ve got a natural moment, write something personal on a cup—a name or a detail from the conversation, not just a smiley. We’re short today, so don’t add pressure when you’re covering positions or the line builds; just focus on taking care of each other and the customers.
managers.private_thought: I want customers to feel seen, but making one more thing mandatory while we’re down a partner would cost more in goodwill than it gains.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate's encouraging notes on cups when you can make them personal, so feel free to add one if there's a natural moment. We're covering an extra spot today, so don't let it slow service down.

managers.message_to_team: The memo asks us to make the notes personal, so while it’s calm, please add something specific for customers you know or have chatted with—not just a smiley. managers.message_to_team: If you’ve got a clean moment, make the cup note personal—name or something from the order, not just a smiley. Don’t let it slow the line or pull someone off the extra position; skip it when we get busy.
